✅ Answer: C. April 30.
The OSHA 300A summary of last year's work-related injuries and illnesses must be posted from February 1 to April 30, even if there were no recordable cases. (Employers with 10 or fewer employees and some low-hazard industries are generally exempt from keeping these records.)

posts.alt_q:
SHRM-CP & SCP Question of the Day: Employers must post the OSHA Form 300A injury and illness summary starting February 1. Until when must it stay posted?
A. March 1
B. March 31
C. April 30
D. December 31
posts.alt_a: Answer: C. April 30. Post last year's summary from February 1 to April 30 where employee notices usually go, even if there were zero cases.

youtube_quiz.explanation: OSHA requires the Form 300A summary to be posted from February 1 to April 30, even with zero recordable cases.

posts.label: EXAM TIP
posts.headline: Beware the extreme answer.
posts.body: "Fire them today." "Ignore it." "Cancel the policy now." On scenario questions these are usually traps. The best answer is often the measured step: get the facts, then act.
posts.caption_instagram:

When an option sounds dramatic (fire them today, scrap the policy, ignore it), slow down. SHRM's best answer is usually the calm, fair step: gather the facts, check the policy, then act. ⚖️

posts.headline: FMLA military caregiver leave allows up to how many weeks in 12 months?
posts.explain: Caring for a covered servicemember with a serious injury or illness? Eligible employees get up to 26 workweeks in a single 12-month period.
posts.facebook_first_comment:
✅ Answer: D. 26 weeks.
Most FMLA leave caps at 12 workweeks, but military caregiver leave allows up to 26 workweeks in a single 12-month period to care for a covered servicemember with a serious injury or illness. The 26 is a combined cap, so any other FMLA leave taken in that period counts toward it.
📚 More practice: https://shrm.thegreygym.com
posts.alt_q:
SHRM-CP & SCP Question of the Day: Under the FMLA, military caregiver leave allows an eligible employee up to how many workweeks of leave in a single 12-month period?
A. 12 weeks
B. 16 weeks
C. 20 weeks
D. 26 weeks
posts.alt_a: Answer: D. 26 weeks. Eligible employees caring for a covered servicemember with a serious injury or illness can take up to 26 workweeks in a single 12-month period.

youtube_quiz.question: Under the FMLA, military caregiver leave allows an eligible employee up to how many workweeks in a single 12-month period?
youtube_quiz.explanation: Military caregiver leave allows up to 26 workweeks in a single 12-month period (combined with other FMLA leave), vs. the usual 12.

sources: U.S. DOL elaws: FMLA military caregiver leave

🎬 Can a job ever legally require a certain sex, religion or national origin?

Only under a BFOQ (bona fide occupational qualification), a very narrow exception to EEO law. The employer has to show it's essential to doing the job. Under Title VII, race and color can never be a BFOQ. 📌

posts.headline: OWBPA, one-person exit: how long must a worker 40+ get to review a release?
posts.explain: One-person exit: at least 21 days to consider the release (45 in a group layoff), plus 7 days to revoke after signing.
posts.facebook_first_comment:
✅ Answer: C. 21 days.
For a valid ADEA waiver in an individual termination, the Older Workers Benefit Protection Act requires at least 21 days to consider the release. In a group layoff or exit incentive program it's 45 days. Either way, the employee then has 7 days to revoke after signing.
📚 More practice: https://shrm.thegreygym.com
posts.alt_q:
SHRM-CP & SCP Question of the Day: Under the OWBPA, an employee age 40 or older is offered severance in exchange for a release in an individual termination. How long must they be given to consider it?
A. 7 days
B. 14 days
C. 21 days
D. 45 days
posts.alt_a: Answer: C. 21 days. In a one-person exit, the employee gets at least 21 days to consider the release (45 in a group layoff), plus 7 days to revoke after signing.

youtube_quiz.question: Under the OWBPA, an employee 40+ is offered severance for a release in an individual termination. How long must they get to consider it?
youtube_quiz.explanation: Individual termination: at least 21 days to consider (45 for a group program), then 7 days to revoke after signing.

sources: 29 CFR 1625.22: Waivers of rights and claims under the ADEA (Cornell LII)
